**On attribution:** the Bible Hub and StudyLight pages that collect many commentaries name some writers and not others. When the excerpt doesn't name the commentator, I say "an unnamed commentator on this page."

## Matthew 10:22–42: Research notes

**v. 22**
- **Guzik (Enduring Word):** You need a commitment to "endure to the end" to get through persecution. Christians who face little persecution understand little of how hard that is. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-10/
- **Matthew Henry:** The troubles will end. While they last they can be borne, because God holds the sufferer up. Salvation is the reward for those who endure. Henry adds that people who endure only for a while and then fall away have "run in vain" and lose what they had gained. Only those who persevere are sure of the prize. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Mat/Mat_010.cfm
- **Gill:** The disciples' sufferings will have an end: at death, at the end of time, or when Jerusalem is destroyed and their enemies are removed. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/matthew-10.html
- **Ellicott:** "Saved" here means salvation in its fullest sense, a full share in the blessings of Christ's kingdom. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/matthew/10.htm
- **Alford:** The words look ahead to the Lord's final coming. "Saved" means everlasting salvation, and "the end" is the end of the Christian's whole life. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hac/matthew-10.html
- **Where traditions differ (whether a true believer can fall away):**
  - *Baptist / Reformed (Spurgeon, sermon hosted on monergism.com):* Perseverance is "the badge of true saints." No true child of God can lose salvation. People who go back to their old life show they were never truly rescued. Spurgeon also says it is to Christ's honour that He makes all His people persevere. https://www.monergism.com/perseverance-enduring-end-matthew-1022 ; also https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/spe/matthew-10.html
  - *Precept Austin (evangelical):* Endurance does not earn salvation. It shows that a person is a genuine, born-again disciple. Precept Austin compares the good soil in the parable of the sower, which bears fruit "with perseverance." https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-10-commentary
  - *JFB:* Falling away "unto perdition" is visible evidence that faith had no root from the start. Enduring is the evidence that it was real. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Mat/Mat_010.cfm
  - *Wesleyan:* StudyLight labels Wesley's Notes "Arminian," but the excerpts I could see had no comment from Wesley on this verse. I can't report a Wesleyan reading of it. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/wes/matthew/10-22.html

**v. 23**
- **Fleeing persecution:**
  - *Guzik:* Jesus taught that it is wrong to *seek out* martyrdom. If an honourable escape is possible, disciples should take it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-10/
  - *Ellicott:* Fleeing is one form of being "wise as serpents." Seeking out martyrdom is not "enduring to the end." Ellicott says Polycarp and Cyprian followed this counsel during Roman persecutions. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/matthew-10.html ; https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-23.htm
  - *Matthew Henry:* In serious danger, disciples may flee when God opens a way out, but they must not leave the path of duty or use sinful means to escape. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/10-33.html ; https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-23.htm
  - *Gill:* The main point is not personal safety. It is to keep preaching and carry the gospel further. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-23.htm
  - *Spurgeon:* The disciples should move on rather than fight local officials. Religion cannot be forced on people; it spreads by gentleness. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-10-commentary-spurgeon
- **"Before the Son of Man comes"** is one of the most debated phrases in the passage. The readings found:
  - *Destruction of Jerusalem (AD 70):*
    - JFB: Christ's coming in judgment on Israel, which foreshadowed His second coming. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-23.htm
    - Carson, quoted by Guzik: "the Son of Man comes in judgment on Israel." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-10/
    - An unnamed commentator on the Bible Hub page reads it as the end of the Jewish system, about thirty years later. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-23.htm
  - *Resurrection or Pentecost:* Gill says it does not mean the second coming. It means either Christ's resurrection or the outpouring of the Spirit at Pentecost. Another unnamed commentator on the page lists all three options (Jerusalem's fall, the resurrection, Pentecost). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-23.htm
  - *Final coming, but foreshortened:* Ellicott admits this naturally led the apostles to expect Christ's return in their lifetime. He links it to the fall of Jerusalem as a type of the final Advent. He suggests the long gap was hidden from them because they could not yet bear it (John 16:12). https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/matthew-10.html
  - *A sharp difficulty:* Barclay says that taken at face value the saying predicts something that did not happen. Yet it is so unlike anything anyone would invent that Jesus must have said it. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/10-34.html ; https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dsb/matthew-10.html
  - *Mission to Israel until the end:* William Kelly says the passage is entirely about Israel. It skips over the Church age and points to a mission to Israel that continues until Christ comes in glory. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/10-28.html

**v. 24–25**
- **Guzik:** Disciples shouldn't expect better treatment than Jesus got. If they called Him Beelzebul (Satan), they will treat His followers worse. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-10/
- **Wesley:** "How much more" can't mean the servant gets more abuse than his master. It means the abuse is even more certain to come. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/matthew-10.html
- **Matthew Henry:** The apostles, who tore down the devil's kingdom, were themselves accused of being devils. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Mat/Mat_010.cfm

**v. 26**
- **Guzik:** Disciples can be bold because the truth will win out in the end. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-10/
- **Wesley:** They are only getting the same treatment as their Lord. Their innocence will eventually be shown, however much they are slandered now. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/matthew-10.html
- **Pulpit Commentary (Homiletics):** Hidden things will be revealed. A life that seems to end in darkness will be vindicated. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/homiletics/matthew/10.htm

**v. 27**
- **Wesley:** Two Jewish customs lie behind this. Rabbis whispered to their students what the students were to say aloud, and people sometimes preached from the low flat roofs of houses. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/matthew-10.html
- **Pulpit Commentary:** The apostles received the teaching privately as stewards, to pass it on, not to keep it. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/matthew-10.html
- **A devotional use (Precept Austin):** The Lord leads people into "the dark," such as grief, loneliness and disappointment, in order to tell them His secrets. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-10-commentary
- **Guzik:** If fear of persecution silences us, Satan has won something without harming us at all. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-10/

**v. 28**
- **Who is "the One" to fear? Commentators agree it is God, not Satan.**
  - Chuck Smith says Satan has no power to destroy the soul in hell.
  - The Light of Israel commentary admits it once wrongly thought the verse meant the devil.

  https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/10-28.html
- **Wesley:** It is striking that Jesus tells people who love God to still fear Him in this way. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/matthew-10.html
- **Gill:** The soul is immortal and lives on after death. God will raise the body and reunite it with the soul. Gill also says God is to be feared not just chiefly but "solely." https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/10-28.html
- **On the nature of hell:**
  - Barnes: The verse shows that the bodies of the wicked will be raised to be punished forever. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/10-28.html
  - JFB: Punishment will affect both the body and the spirit, and both will exist forever. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Mat/Mat_010.cfm
  - Alford: "Destroy" can only mean eternal destruction. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hac/matthew-10.html
  - Barclay puts it differently: God can condemn a person to "the death of the soul." https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/10-27.html
- **Word note:** The Greek word for hell here is *Gehenna*, the Valley of Hinnom near Jerusalem, which became a name for the place of final punishment. https://biblehub.com/matthew/10-28.htm

**v. 29–31**
- **Guzik:** If God cares for sparrows and counts our hairs, He pays close attention to our needs. Persecuted people easily feel forgotten, but they are not. Guzik also quotes a remark that this is the third "do not fear" in six verses. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-10/
- **Wesley:** God's providence reaching even the smallest things is a further reason not to fear people. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/matthew-10.html
- **Matthew Henry:** This is not for curious speculation. It is encouragement to depend on God's care for everything that happens. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Mat/Mat_010.cfm
- **Spurgeon:** It's "a sermon against fear" with sparrows as the text. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-10-commentary-spurgeon
- **Precept Austin:** Sparrows were worth almost nothing. If God notices one fall, He feels every pain of His children. https://temp.preceptaustin.org/index.php/matthew-10-commentary

**v. 32**
- **Guzik:** Confessing Christ means doing it publicly. Jesus makes a person's eternal destiny depend on how they respond to Him, which shows He is more than a prophet. https://enduringword.com/you-must-confess/
- **Wesley:** Confessing Him means publicly acknowledging Him as the Messiah. That includes accepting all His teaching and obeying all His commands. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/matthew-10.html
- **Matthew Henry:** We honour Christ before people, which is a small thing. He honours us before the Father, which is a great thing. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/10-34.html

**v. 33**
- **What kind of denial is meant?**
  - Matthew Henry: Only a denial that a person *persists in*. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-23.htm
  - William MacDonald (on Precept Austin): Not a brief denial under pressure, like Peter's, but a denial that is habitual and final. https://temp.preceptaustin.org/index.php/matthew-10-commentary
  - Alford: Lasting, practical denial. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hac/matthew-10.html
  - Bob Utley stresses the seriousness: what we decide now carries into eternity (compare 2 Tim 2:12). https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-10-commentary
- **Wesley:** Disciples will be strongly tempted to deny Him. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/10.htm

**v. 34**
- **Purpose vs. result.** Most writers say division is the *result* of Christ's coming, not its *goal*:
  - Barnes: Human wickedness, not the gospel, causes the hostility. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-34.htm
  - Wesley: Division "is not the design, though it be the event" of His coming. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/10.htm
  - Precept Austin: "distinguish between the purpose... and the result." https://temp.preceptaustin.org/index.php/matthew-10-commentary
  - *A dissenting reading:* An unnamed commentator on the Bible Hub page (writing on the Greek) says it is a real but secondary purpose. The conflict is a necessary stage the Messiah has to bring about. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-34.htm
- **Gill:** The Jews, and the disciples too, expected outward peace and prosperity when the Messiah came. Christ gives peace with God, but not peace in the world. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-34.htm
- **Ellicott:** He links the verse to Simeon's words to Mary that a sword would pierce her soul (Luke 2:35). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-34.htm
- **Pulpit Commentary:** Peace grows from the inside out. What Christ throws onto the earth is fire and a sword. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/matthew-10.html
- **Vincent:** The Greek verb means "to throw," as if the disciples were looking up waiting for peace to drop from heaven. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-34.htm
- **Precept Austin:** Jesus corrects the hope for a conquering Messiah who would beat Rome. The sword is a picture of division, not a real weapon. https://temp.preceptaustin.org/index.php/matthew-10-commentary
- **Lutheran (1517.org):** Division is the result of preaching, not its purpose, and Jesus is not out to destroy the family. https://www.1517.org/articles/gospel-matthew-1034-42-pentecost-4-series-a
- **Catholic (catholic.com):** Gives a "mystical" reading, set out under v. 35–36. https://www.catholic.com/qa/the-explanation-of-not-peace-but-a-sword

**v. 35–36**
- **Barnes:** The words come from Micah 7:6. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-34.htm
- **Precept Austin:** Believing in Him, or rejecting Him, will split even close families. https://temp.preceptaustin.org/index.php/matthew-10-commentary
- **Wesley:** Public and private divisions follow wherever the gospel comes with power. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/matthew-10.html
- **Barclay:** It is as if God stepping into history is splitting families in two. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/10-34.html
- **Catholic (catholic.com):**
  - In baptism the word, like God's sword, cuts the new person off from inherited sin and old desires. That causes conflict "in one house."
  - "Daughter-in-law against mother-in-law" is read as the Church against the Synagogue.

  https://www.catholic.com/qa/the-explanation-of-not-peace-but-a-sword

**v. 37**
- **Lutheran (1517.org):** Jesus does not destroy the family. He puts it in its place below Himself and His cross. This applies the greatest commandment to family life. The article points to Abraham and Isaac as an example. https://www.1517.org/articles/gospel-matthew-1034-42-pentecost-4-series-a
- **Wesley:** It means anyone not ready to give these up when they compete with duty. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/matthew-10.html
- **Pulpit Commentary:** Christ's claims come first. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-34.htm

**v. 38**
- **Guzik:** Taking up your cross isn't carrying your particular trial. It is death to self, with no bargaining and resurrection life as the only hope. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-10/
- **Precept Austin:** We must pick the cross up willingly, not drag it: "carried crosses grow light." https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-10-commentary
- **JFB:** Our Lord repeats this saying several times (Matt 16:24; Luke 9:23; 14:27). https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Mat/Mat_010.cfm

**v. 39**
- **Guzik:** Calls this the central paradox of the kingdom. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-10/
- **Pulpit Commentary:** Everything in the hereafter depends on how we respond to Christ's claims. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/10-34.htm

**v. 40**
- **Bridgeway Bible Commentary:** Welcoming Jesus' messengers is welcoming Jesus, and the Father who sent Him. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/10-23.html

**v. 41**
- **Wesley:** "Prophet" here means a preacher of the gospel. Whoever receives one *because* he is a preacher shares his reward. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/matthew-10.html
- **A. T. Pierson (on Precept Austin):** The Jews ranked the prophet's reward highest. Whoever helps a prophet speak for God shares that reward. Making his work harder loses it, so look past a speaker's manner to his message. https://temp.preceptaustin.org/index.php/matthew-10-commentary

**v. 42**
- **Guzik:** God notices and rewards even the smallest kindness. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-10/
- **Spurgeon:** Every kind act is its own reward, but God promises more. "Truly I tell you" and "in no wise" rule out any loss. Giving help is also a way of fellowship with the saints, especially when governments punish it. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-10-commentary-spurgeon
- **Bridgeway:** Help given to Jesus' messengers is rewarded as if given to Jesus Himself. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/10-23.html
- **Barclay:** He tells of a cobbler whose service, he says, will be rewarded like a preacher's. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/10-34.html

---

**Not found (left out as you asked):**
- Pentecostal or charismatic teaching specific to this passage. Guzik is the only enduringword.com source, and he gives no distinctly Pentecostal reading here.
- Reformed sources other than the Spurgeon sermon hosted on monergism.com.
- Wesley's comments on v. 22, 24, 29–31, 36, 38–40 and 42. For several of these the excerpts showed only the verse text or a joint note on nearby verses, with no comment of his own.
- Modern scholarship (bibleodyssey.org, netbible.org notes).
- Orthodox readings (oca.org), and any Catholic readings beyond v. 34–36.
- Any discussion of prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace teaching on this passage.
- Any annihilationist reading of v. 28.

The next step would be to open the full Enduring Word, Precept Austin and Bible Hub verse pages, and to run targeted searches on netbible.org, newadvent.org (the Catena Aurea) and oca.org.
